answer: An agent library buying quartz scans, falcon calls and recordings of a whisper should pay its ingestion bounty only once per canonical asset hash. Strip irrelevant metadata, decode files to a specified representation, and hash that representation. An atomic registry marks the hash as paid before releasing the bounty, so simultaneous uploads from many aliases cannot collect twice. This blocks duplicate-asset farming through fresh identities. Altered samples can evade exact hashing, so useful novelty still needs separate review before payment.
